title: Banks Act Directive D1/2008 — Use of divisional names
enablingLegislation: Section 6(6)(a) of the Banks Act, 1990 (Act No. 94 of 1990)

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Introduction 1.1 This directive is issued by the Prudential Authority in terms of Section 6(6)(a) of the Banks Act, 1990 (Act No. 94 of 1990). 1.2 Use of divisional names. 1.3 This directive remains effective as confirmed in Banks Act Circular 1 of the relevant year.

subsections.text: This directive is issued by the Prudential Authority in terms of Section 6(6)(a) of the Banks Act, 1990 (Act No. 94 of 1990).
This directive remains effective as confirmed in Banks Act Circular 1 of the relevant year.

sections.heading: Application
sections.text: Application 2.1 This directive applies to all banks, branches of foreign institutions and controlling companies registered or operating in South Africa in terms of the Banks Act, 1990 (Act No. 94 of 1990). 2.2 Institutions are required to ensure compliance with the requirements set out herein.

subsections.text: This directive applies to all banks, branches of foreign institutions and controlling companies registered or operating in South Africa in terms of the Banks Act, 1990 (Act No. 94 of 1990).
Institutions are required to ensure compliance with the requirements set out herein.

sections.heading: Acknowledgement of receipt
sections.text: Acknowledgement of receipt 3.1 Kindly ensure that a copy of this directive is made available to your institution's auditors. The attached acknowledgement of receipt, duly completed and signed by both the Chief Executive Officer of the institution and the said auditors, must be returned to the PA at the earliest convenience of the aforementioned signatories.
